sections.h2: What the Cabarrus County register files and keeps
sections.html:
This is the office that records your deed, your buyer's deed of trust and every release or assignment tied to the property, and keeps them as public record. The register is the legal custodian for recording, indexing, storing and preserving land documents, birth, death and marriage records, veteran discharges, notary records, subdivision maps and condominium plans.

Counter staff only record. State law bars them from practicing law, so expect no blank forms, no coaching on how to fill one in, and no opinion on what a signed instrument means for you. Drafting normally falls to your closing attorney.

Once recorded, every page is open to public viewing. Do not put a Social Security number or bank account number on anything you submit.

sections.h2: Why recording time matters to a seller
sections.html:
The clock stamp decides priority. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance protects the buyer against lien creditors and later purchasers for value only once it is registered in the county where the land lies, and the order of registration sets who comes first. Since the counter stops taking filings at 4:30, ask your attorney when the package is due to arrive.

Two habits save trouble. Confirm that the payoff of your old mortgage has been released, because a satisfaction of a deed of trust carries no recording fee under state law, but it still has to be filed. Have the attorney confirm that each owner named on the deed has signed and that the property description copies your earlier deed.

The filing window is weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., and recording fees are paid by cash or check only. Credit cards are not accepted for recording fees, which catches out sellers who expect to settle every charge by card at the counter.

After you bring or mail in a document, the office follows a fixed routine:

  • Staff check that the document can be recorded and work out the correct fee
  • It is stamped with the date and time, then given a document number, book and page
  • It is indexed in the computer system
  • Each day the documents are imaged, and a copy goes to the NC Department of Archives for backup
  • The processed document is returned to the proper party by the next day

That one-day return helps if a buyer's lender is waiting on proof of recording.

A deed, release or other general instrument costs $26 for 15 pages with $4 added per further page. A mortgage or deed of trust costs $64 for 35 pages with the same $4 add-on. Both sit inside the uniform statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10.

Cabarrus County recording fees
DocumentFee
Deeds, trustee deeds, releases, assignments, powers of attorney$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Plats (mylar, 18 x 24 inches only)$21 per sheet
Subsequent instrument citing more than one original$10 for each added reference
Nonstandard document$25 on top of the recording fee

The $25 nonstandard fee applies when paper size, margins, ink or type fall short of G.S. 161-14. The checklist asks for letter or legal paper, a blank band three inches deep at the top of page one, black ink on one side only and type no smaller than 10 point. The fee does not apply to a document whose notary acknowledgement predates July 1, 2002.

The stamp is $2 for each $1,000 of purchase price, added to the recording charge and divided equally between Cabarrus County and the state. The statute behind it is G.S. 105-228.30, which puts the cost on the person transferring title and prices it per $500 of value.

Since the register takes only cash or check for recording fees, plan how the seller's side will be funded at the closing table. Most sellers have the closing attorney deduct the stamp from proceeds, so ask for the figure early and confirm who will deliver the payment to the office.

The register runs an online records search for property data, and the office's remote site holds indexes and document images from 1792 to the present, plus all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps.

The county partners with Logan Systems to redact Social Security and driver's license numbers from the internet copy, beginning with records from 1935. For older documents, the office has a Public Records Redaction Request form. The register files only fixture-related UCC statements, and everything else in that category goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

If a title search for your sale turns up an old lien or easement, the index is where a closing attorney will trace it.

The office handles a few side tasks that often come up around a sale or an estate. It files military discharges at no charge when you bring the original or a military copy with a raised seal, and only the person the statute allows may record or obtain a copy. Discharges that have been on file for 80 years or longer are public, while newer ones carry restricted access.

It also swears in new notaries, collecting a $10 oath fee, with no appointment needed once the Secretary of State's notice arrives. Copies of birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage license applications are available through the county's records pages, which helps heirs who need certificates to settle an inherited house.

Cabarrus is a fast-growing Piedmont county northeast of Charlotte, with Concord as the county seat. The population is 249,725, up 10.6% from the April 2020 base, with 100,316 housing units and an owner-occupied rate of 71.2%. The median owner-occupied home is worth $354,800 and median gross rent is $1,414.

Plan your closing around the 4:30 recording cutoff, and have your attorney confirm the fee, the stamp tax and the payment method before the package goes in.

If you are bringing a deed yourself, check the page count against the fee table, make sure the paper meets the format checklist, and carry a check or cash, since cards are not taken. A deed that is ready and correctly formatted usually comes back the next day with its document number, book and page, which your buyer's lender may ask to see.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file a deed with the Cabarrus County office?
faqs.a: Fifteen pages run $26, and each page beyond that adds $4. On top of that come the excise stamp, which the county lists at $2 per $1,000 of price, and a $25 surcharge if the paper or print misses the state format rules.

faqs.q: Will the Cabarrus County office take a card for recording fees?
faqs.a: No. Recording fees must be paid by cash or check, and credit cards are not accepted. Your closing attorney can usually handle the payment from the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: What hours does Cabarrus County accept documents for recording?
faqs.a: Weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Finished documents are sent back to the proper party by the following day.

faqs.q: Can the Cabarrus County staff tell me what my deed should say?
faqs.a: No. The office acts as a recording office only, and North Carolina law prohibits staff from practicing law. They cannot supply legal forms, instruct you on completing them, or explain legal effects, so see an attorney.

faqs.q: How far back do Cabarrus County online records go?
faqs.a: The register's remote site has indexes and images from 1792 to the present, along with all subdivision plats, condominium plats and NC right-of-way maps. Redaction of personal numbers online begins with 1935 records, and older ones need a redaction request form.
